name: Summer 2025 Riverine Flood Scenario
location: Sindh, Punjab, and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP), Pakistan
impact: Widespread inundation across 2.2 million people in the exposure zone, affecting critical infrastructure including 30 hospitals, 45 schools, 18 bridges, and 780 km of roads. High risk of localized cloud bursts in the Kirthar Range.
context: A convergence of climatic factors including La Niña development, a positive Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD), and elevated Tibetan Plateau temperatures is driving heavy monsoon rains and glacial melt. The scenario culminates in peak river flows coinciding with Tarbela Dam reaching maximum reservoir capacity. The disaster event is projected for 27th July to 3rd August 2025, with the most severe impacts concentrated in the Lower Indus basin.
